'''Health and environment'''
*[[2020–22 North American drought]]
**[[Lake Mead]] drops to its lowest water level ever recorded. [https://www.msn.com/en-gb/news/world/lake-mead-largest-us-reservoir-falls-to-historic-low-amid-devastating-drought/ar-AAKVf7H?ocid=uxbndlbing (MSN)] 
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pennsylvania]]
*****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Philadelphia]]
******[[Philadelphia]] lifts its [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] and COVID-19 restrictions. However, people who are not fully vaccinated are encouraged to wear masks. [https://www.abc27.com/news/health/coronavirus/philadelphia-joins-other-cities-lifting-mask-mandates/ (WHTM-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Jersey]]
*****[[New Jersey]] reports 400 hospitalizations due to COVID-19, the lowest number in eight months. [https://www.nj.com/coronavirus/2021/06/nj-reports-4-covid-deaths-194-cases-hospitalizations-fall-below-400-patients-for-1st-time-in-8-months.html (NJ)]
****The death toll from COVID-19 surpasses 600,000. The United States accounts for 16% of COVID-related deaths worldwide. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/health/2021/06/11/600000-covid-deaths-us/ (''The Washington Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba]]
*****[[Manitoba]] surpasses one million doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] administered. [https://winnipeg.ctvnews.ca/manitoba-crosses-covid-19-vaccine-milestone-expands-second-dose-eligibility-1.5466717 (CTV News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****Fully vaccinated [[senior citizen]]s will be permitted to go out in areas placed under the [[COVID-19 community quarantines in the Philippines|General Community Quarantine]] and [[COVID-19 community quarantines in the Philippines|Modified General Community Quarantine]]. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/fully-vaccinated-senior-citizens-allowed-go-out-gcq-mgcq-june-11-2021 (Rappler)]
****The [[Inter-Agency Task Force for the Management of Emerging Infectious Diseases]] announces that gyms, museums, and other establishments in the [[Greater Manila Area]] will be allowed to reopen. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/06/11/21/gyms-museums-open-ncr-plus-iatf?fbclid=IwAR24CDWpXOfnpUVpTTuPnWwm32A5vUgxIcjCswASdCeyH_Tb6dtOunsvNCU (ABS-CBN News and Current Affairs)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]], [[Malaysian movement control order]]
****The [[Government of Malaysia|government]] announces the extension of its nationwide total [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] for another two weeks from June 15 to June 28 as the number of [[COVID-19]] cases in the country continues to remain high. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/covid-19-malaysia-total-lockdown-extend-two-weeks-jun-15-jun-28-14993456 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] surpasses 2,000 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19 after a record 101 deaths are reported in the past 24 hours. [https://m.timesofindia.com/world/south-asia/sri-lanka-records-highest-single-day-covid-19-death-toll/amp_articleshow/83429387.cms (''The Times of India'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
*****The [[Robert Koch Institute]] removes dozens of countries, including the [[United States]], [[Canada]], [[Austria]], and [[Lebanon]], from its travel risk list due to low COVID-19 infection rates. [[Minister for Foreign Affairs (Germany)|Foreign Minister]] [[Heiko Maas]] later announces that most of the countries still on the list will be removed on July 1. [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-takes-us-canada-off-travel-risk-list-most-others-from-july/a-57851397 (Deutsche Welle)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Italy]]
*****[[Italy]] suspends the use of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] vaccine in people under the age of 60 nationwide following the death of an 18-year-old girl yesterday and reports of other young people who have been hospitalized in critical condition after receiving their first dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. The [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna]] and [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer]] vaccines will be used for the vaccination of people under the age of 60, including for people who already received a first dose of the AstraZeneca vaccine. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/06/11/us-health-coronavirus-italy-astrazeneca (Euronews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] reports its first case of the [[Lineage P.1]] [[SARS-CoV-2 Gamma variant|Gamma variant]] that originated in [[Brazil]]. [https://greekreporter.com/2021/06/11/first-case-of-brazilian-coronavirus-variant-in-greece/ (Greek Reporter)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports 12,505 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest daily total since February, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 5.18 million. [https://www.reuters.com/world/russia-records-highest-daily-covid-cases-since-february-2021-06-11/ (Reuters)] 
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 lockdowns|Lockdown]] restrictions are eased in [[Melbourne]] after a decrease in [[COVID-19]] cases. Schools and businesses reopen in a limited capacity. People are allowed to travel up to {{cvt|25|km}} from their homes and hold public gatherings of up to 10 people. However, most home visits remain banned and masks are still mandatory in indoor settings. Restrictions are eased further in regional [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]], where [[gym]]s are reopened and private gatherings of up to two people and public gatherings of up to 20 people are allowed. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/jun/10/melbourne-lockdown-covid-victoria-restrictions-coronavirus-rules-covid19-explained-10km-radius-masks-compulsory-exercising-home-gatherings-what-you-need-to-know (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2019–2021 polio outbreak in the Philippines]]
**The [[World Health Organization]] and [[UNICEF]] declare the end of the [[polio]] epidemic in the [[Philippines]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/asiapacific/2021-06/11/c_1310002774.htm (Xinhua News Agency)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 United Nations Security Council election]]
**[[Gabon]], the [[United Arab Emirates]], [[Brazil]], [[Ghana]] and [[Albania]] are elected non-permanent members of the [[United Nations Security Council]] for the 2022–2023 term. [https://www.reuters.com/world/albania-brazil-gabon-ghana-uae-elected-un-security-council-2021-06-11/ (Reuters)]
*[[Malawi–South Africa relations]]
**The [[Department of International Relations and Cooperation|South Africa Department of International Relations]] orders several [[Malawi]]an diplomats and their families to leave within 72 hours after [[South African Police Service|police]] found they were illegally selling duty-free alcohol. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/12/south-africa-expels-malawi-diplomats-over-booze-scandal (Al Jazeera English)]
*The [[47th G7 summit]] begins in [[Cornwall]], [[England]]. It will run until June 13. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/06/10/the-g-7-summit-guide-to-everything-you-need-to-know.html (CNBC)]
*Former [[Vice President of Costa Rica|Costa Rican Vice President]] [[Rebeca Grynspan]] is named the new Secretary-General of the [[United Nations Conference on Trade and Development]]. [https://unctad.org/news/rebeca-grynspan-appointed-unctads-secretary-general (United Nations Conference on Trade and Development)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 United States Capitol attack]]
**[[Chicago Police Department|Chicago Police]] officer Karol Chwiesiuk is arrested for allegedly breaking into [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Jeff Merkley]] ([[Democratic Party (United States)|D]]-[[Oregon|OR]])'s office during the [[2021 United States Capitol attack|attack]] on the [[United States Capitol]]. [https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/criminal-justice/ct-chicago-police-officer-capitol-breach-federal-charges-20210611-dof6a7g6wrf5be2w3wsdjurbje-story.html (''Chicago Tribune'')]
*[[Amnesty International]] reports that [[Algeria]]n authorities arrested two journalists and a prominent activist days before [[2021 Algerian legislative election|the legislation election]], as part of a wider crackdown on [[2019–2021 Algerian protests|Hirak]] supporters. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/11/algeria-arrests-prominent-journalists-activist-before-election (Al Jazeera English)]
*Security research firm [[NordLocker]] publishes a report on an anonymous trojan virus program that has stolen 1.2 terabytes of login credential information and personally identifiable information from 26 million users between 2018 and 2020.  The login credentials were stored in a cloud database and ranged across a large selection of website types from almost a million websites including [[Amazon_(company)|Amazon]], [[eBay]], [[Facebook]], [[Twitter]], [[Walmart]], [[Apple_Inc.|Apple]], [[Paypal]], [[Gmail]], [[Netflix]], and [[Steam_(service)|Steam]].  The malware also targeted stored files in desktops and Downloads folders. Over 6 million files were stolen, with 50% being text files, 1 million images, and 650,000 Word or PDF files. The malware also took screenshots and images of users with their own webcams. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/money/other/nearly-26m-amazon-facebook-apple-ebay-user-logins-stolen-by-hackers/ar-AAKXasT (MSN)] [https://www.foxbusiness.com/technology/hackers-logins-amazon-facebook-apple-ebay (Fox Business)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Peruvian general election]]
**[[Vladimir Cerrón]], leader of the [[socialist]] [[Free Peru]] party, claims victory for leftist candidate [[Pedro Castillo]] as vote counting approaches an end with more than 99.5% of votes counted and with Castillo more than 60,000 votes ahead of [[right-wing]] candidate [[Keiko Fujimori]]. Some countries in the region have already congratulated Castillo on his apparent presidential election win. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/perus-socialist-party-chief-cites-victory-vote-count-nears-end-2021-06-11/ (Reuters)]
**The [[Organization of American States]] says that they have found no evidence of voting irregularities in the election. However, they also called for candidates not to be proclaim themselves as winners until all challenges have been resolved. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-57439548 (BBC News)]
*[[Viktor Sheiman]], who served as [[Chief of Staff to the President of Belarus|head]] of the [[Presidential Administration of Belarus]], resigns. [[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] accepts his resignation. [https://eng.belta.by/president/view/belarus-president-property-management-directorate-heads-resignation-accepted-140795-2021/ (Belarusian Telegraph Agency)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**A group of scientists from [[NASA]]'s [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] and the [[University of New Mexico]] announces that water clouds are discovered on [[TOI-1231 b]], a [[Neptune]]-like [[exoplanet]] that is located 90 [[Light-year|light-years]] away from [[Earth]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/astronomers-discover-neptune-exoplanet-water-clouds/ (CBS News)]
*[[COVID-19 misinformation]]
**[[YouTube]] announces that it has temporarily suspended U.S. Senator [[Ron Johnson (Wisconsin politician)|Ron Johnson]] ([[Republican Party (United States)|R]]-[[Wisconsin|WI]]) for violating its policies about promoting unproven alternative therapies to treat COVID-19. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/youtube-suspends-gop-sen-ron-johnson-s-account-says-he-n1270569 (NBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*The investigation into [[Gansu ultramarathon disaster]] in China, which resulted in 21 died of [[hypothermia]] in May 2021, is released. Investigators say the incident was caused by extreme weather and unprofessional organization. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/12/deadly-china-ultramarathon-leads-to-suicide-arrests (Al Jazeera English)]
*The [[UEFA Euro 2020]] tournament begins with the opening match between [[Italy national football team|Italy]] and [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]] in [[Rome]], ending in a 3–0 victory for Italy. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51135482 (BBC Sport)]
